evidence: src/domain/errors.ts: DomainError base class, with NotFoundError and ConflictError extending it; it is the only error abstraction in the module
src/domain/project.ts and src/domain/user.ts: each constructor checks its own required fields and throws DomainError
src/domain/task-status.ts: TaskStatusValue and TaskStatus.values are the only definition of the allowed statuses; create() validates input and throws DomainError
src/domain/task.ts: Task.markDone checks status.isDone(), throws ConflictError and changes status through TaskStatus.create('done'), so it uses the value object
src/domain/repositories.ts: UserRepository, ProjectRepository and TaskRepository are ports typed with the domain entities; TaskFilters reuses TaskStatusValue instead of redefining the statuses
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The domain module covers one concern: the task-management domain model. It has entities (Project, User, Task), a value object (TaskStatus), the domain error types (DomainError, NotFoundError, ConflictError) and repository interfaces. All validation failures throw DomainError or a subclass, so the error abstraction is used consistently. Task status changes go through TaskStatus.create/isDone, so no raw strings get around the status rules. The allowed status values are defined only in task-status.ts. The 'already done' rule is checked once, in Task.markDone. The required-field checks in Project, User and Task each cover a different entity's fields; they are not copies of one shared invariant. The status values appear in both the TaskStatusValue type and the TaskStatus.values array, but both are in the same file. TaskFilters uses the primitive TaskStatusValue, which is a reasonable choice for a query filter and does not get around the rules. No split, cross-file duplication or bypass was found.
